stem.en:
In her review of the exhibition, the critic acknowledged the painter's technical skill but found the collection ______: nearly every canvas repeated the same muted colors, the same harbor scene, and the same solitary figure, so that by the third room the paintings had begun to blur together.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: monotonous
provocative
eclectic
ambitious

why.en: The colon explains the blank: the same colors, scene and figure repeat until the paintings blur together, so the collection is 'monotonous'. 'Eclectic' means varied.
why.uz: Ikki nuqtadan keyingi qism izoh beradi: bir xil rang, manzara va qahramon takrorlanadi, shuning uchun toʻplam «monotonous» (bir xil). «Eclectic» xilma-xil degani.
why.ru: Часть после двоеточия поясняет: одни и те же цвета, сюжет и фигура повторяются, значит, собрание «monotonous» (однообразно). «Eclectic» значит «разнородный».

stem.en:
Although the agreement between the two neighboring families was praised at the time as a lasting settlement, its wording was so ______ that each family could read it as confirming its own claim to the orchard; within a decade, those same unclear clauses had started a new dispute.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: equivocal
precise
transparent
concise

why.en: Each side could read the wording as supporting itself, and the clauses are called 'unclear', so the wording was 'equivocal' (open to two readings).
why.uz: Har ikki tomon matnni oʻz foydasiga oʻqiy olgan va bandlar «unclear» deyilgan, demak matn «equivocal», yaʼni ikki xil talqin qilinadigan boʻlgan.
why.ru: Каждая сторона читала текст в свою пользу, а пункты названы «unclear», значит, формулировки были «equivocal» (двусмысленными).

stem.en:
Rano had expected the interview to be a formality, a polite conversation before an offer that had all but been decided. The director's questions, however, were pointed and exacting, and Rano soon realized that nothing about the outcome was settled.

As used in the text, what does the word "exacting" most nearly mean?

options.en: demanding
rehearsed
flattering
routine

why.en: 'However' contrasts the questions with a polite formality, and they make Rano unsure of the result, so 'exacting' means 'demanding'.
why.uz: «However» savollarni xushmuomala rasmiyatchilikka qarama-qarshi qoʻyadi va ular Ranoni ikkilantiradi, demak «exacting» «talabchan» degani.
why.ru: «However» противопоставляет вопросы вежливой формальности, и они заставляют Рано сомневаться, значит, «exacting» — «требовательный».

stem.en:
The editor's comments on the manuscript were ______: rather than rewriting the author's sentences, she marked only the few places where the argument lost its thread and trusted the author to repair them herself.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: sparing
exhaustive
dismissive
illegible

why.en: She marked only a few places and did not rewrite, so her comments were few: 'sparing'. 'Exhaustive' is the opposite, and trusting the author is not 'dismissive'.
why.uz: U faqat bir necha joyni belgilagan va qayta yozmagan, demak izohlar kam: «sparing». «Exhaustive» buning aksi, muallifga ishonish esa «dismissive» emas.
why.ru: Она отметила лишь несколько мест и ничего не переписывала, значит, замечаний мало: «sparing». «Exhaustive» — противоположность, а доверие автору — не «dismissive».

stem.en:
The council's decision to delay the vote was widely seen as ______. Members insisted that they needed more time to study the budget, but critics pointed out that the delay conveniently pushed the issue past the upcoming election.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: calculated
impartial
impulsive

why.en: Critics suggest the delay was planned to gain an advantage (pushing the issue past the election), so it was seen as 'calculated', not 'impulsive'.
why.uz: Tanqidchilar kechiktirish foyda uchun oldindan oʻylangan deb hisoblaydi (masala saylovdan keyinga qoldi), shuning uchun u «calculated» deb qabul qilingan.
why.ru: Критики считают, что отсрочку спланировали ради выгоды (вопрос ушёл за выборы), поэтому её сочли «calculated» (расчётливой), а не «impulsive».

stem.en:
The following text is from a poem.

My grandmother's hands knew the dough by heart:
the press, the fold, the turn, the rest.
She never measured, never weighed;
each loaf was what her fingers guessed.
Now I bake from a careful card,
each gram in ink, each minute timed,
and every loaf comes out correct,
and none of them are quite like hers.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It contrasts a relative's instinctive baking with the speaker's exact but less satisfying approach.
It lists the steps for making bread by hand and then explains why the speaker decided to change one of them.
It recalls a failed attempt at baking and then describes how the speaker finally succeeded.
It praises written recipes and then criticizes cooks who refuse to use them.

why.en: The first half shows the grandmother baking by feel; 'Now' turns to the speaker's measured baking, whose loaves are 'correct' but not like hers.
why.uz: Birinchi qismda buvi his bilan non yopadi; «Now» soʻzidan keyin soʻzlovchining oʻlchab yopishi keladi: non «correct», lekin buvinikidek emas.
why.ru: Первая половина показывает, как бабушка печёт на ощупь; после «Now» — точная выпечка говорящего: хлеб «correct», но не такой, как у неё.

stem.en:
Critics of public libraries sometimes argue that, now that so much information is available online, libraries have become unnecessary. This argument assumes that a library's main purpose is to store information. Yet many of the services libraries offer, such as quiet study space, help from a trained librarian, and free use of computers and printers, have little to do with storing books. A library, in other words, is less a warehouse than a public room.

Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence in the text as a whole?

options.en: It identifies an assumption behind the critics' argument that the rest of the text goes on to challenge.
It offers evidence that supports the critics' claim about online information.
It introduces a concession that the author accepts without any reservation.
It defines a term that the author later argues is no longer useful.

why.en: Sentence 2 names what the critics take for granted (libraries exist to store information); 'Yet' then shows that this assumption is wrong.
why.uz: 2-gap tanqidchilar oʻz-oʻzidan toʻgʻri deb bilgan narsani aytadi (kutubxona maʼlumot saqlash uchun); «Yet» dan keyin bu taxmin rad etiladi.
why.ru: Предложение 2 называет, что критики считают само собой разумеющимся (библиотека хранит информацию); после «Yet» это допущение опровергается.

stem.en:
Tulips are often associated with the Netherlands, where tulip prices rose so wildly between 1634 and 1637 that the episode became known as "tulip mania." Yet the flower's story begins far to the east. The Pamir-Alai and Tien Shan mountains of Central Asia are the center of the wild tulip's diversity, and the first people to cultivate tulips were Turkish and Persian gardeners, long before the flowers reached Dutch markets.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To show that a flower commonly linked to one country began elsewhere
To explain why tulip prices in the Netherlands suddenly fell in 1637
To argue that wild Central Asian tulips are more beautiful than Dutch ones
To describe how Dutch gardeners developed new varieties of tulips

why.en: The text starts with the usual link to the Netherlands, then 'Yet' moves the story east to Central Asia and Turkish and Persian gardeners.
why.uz: Matn lolaning odatda Niderlandiya bilan bogʻlanishidan boshlanadi, soʻng «Yet» hikoyani sharqqa, Markaziy Osiyo va turk, fors bogʻbonlariga olib boradi.
why.ru: Текст начинается с привычной связи с Нидерландами, затем «Yet» переносит историю на восток: в Центральную Азию, к турецким и персидским садовникам.

stem.en:
Text 1
Allowing students to retake tests, some educators argue, encourages them to treat the first attempt carelessly: if a poor score can simply be replaced, there is little reason to prepare seriously the first time. A test should measure what a student knows on a given day, and a retake policy blurs that measurement.

Text 2
Opponents of retakes are right that a policy with no conditions invites careless first attempts. But the remedy is to attach conditions, not to abolish retakes. A student who must correct every error on the first test and attend a review session before retaking it has every reason to prepare, and the second score is a better measure of what the student has actually learned.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that retakes lead to careless first attempts?

options.en: By granting that this happens when retakes are unconditional but arguing that required steps before a retake would prevent it
By rejecting the claim and arguing that students always prepare seriously for a first attempt
By agreeing that retakes should be abolished because they blur what a test measures
By arguing that a first attempt matters more than a retake because it shows knowledge on a given day

why.en: Text 2 says the critics 'are right' about retakes with no conditions, then proposes conditions (correcting errors, a review session) as the remedy.
why.uz: 2-matn shartsiz qayta topshirish haqida tanqidchilar «are right» deydi, keyin yechim sifatida shartlar taklif qiladi (xatolarni tuzatish, takrorlash darsi).
why.ru: Текст 2 признаёт, что критики «are right» насчёт пересдач без условий, и предлагает условия (исправить ошибки, прийти на разбор) как решение.

instructions.ru: Прочитайте оба текста. Определите, как связаны их идеи.

stem.en:
Text 1
A translator of poetry, some argue, owes her first loyalty to the literal meaning of the original. If a translated poem rhymes beautifully but changes what the poet actually said, it is no longer a translation but a new poem wearing the original's name.

Text 2
A poem's meaning does not live only in its words; it lives also in its sound, its rhythm, and the feelings these produce. A translation that keeps every literal meaning but loses the music may be accurate in a narrow sense while failing to convey what made the poem worth reading. The translator's task is to find, in a new language, an effect equivalent to the original's, even if this requires departing from its exact words.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view presented in Text 1?

options.en: By arguing that a strictly literal translation can be unfaithful to the original poem
By agreeing that a translator should never depart from the exact words of the original poem
By claiming that poems cannot be translated into another language at all
By suggesting that in most poems rhyme matters less than the literal meaning of the words

why.en: For Text 2, meaning includes sound and rhythm, so a literal version that 'loses the music' fails the poem: literal is not the same as faithful.
why.uz: 2-matnga koʻra maʼno tovush va ritmni ham oʻz ichiga oladi, shuning uchun «loses the music» boʻlgan soʻzma-soʻz tarjima sheʼrga sodiq emas.
why.ru: Для текста 2 смысл включает звук и ритм, поэтому дословный перевод, который «loses the music», не верен стихотворению.

stem.en:
Bobur's family runs a small bakery in their neighborhood. Every morning, Bobur wakes up at five to help his father shape the bread before school. The work is tiring, but Bobur has learned how to measure flour exactly, how to tell when dough is ready, and how to talk politely with customers. He says these lessons have helped him in his chemistry class and in his school's debate club.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Bobur's work at the bakery has taught him skills that help him at school.
Bobur wants to open a bakery of his own after he finishes school next year.
Bobur finds chemistry class more difficult than working in the bakery.
Bobur's father plans to stop baking bread in the mornings.

why.en: Most of the text lists what Bobur learned at the bakery, and the last sentence links those skills to chemistry and debate.
why.uz: Matnning katta qismi Bobur novvoyxonada nimalarni oʻrganganini sanaydi, oxirgi gap esa bu koʻnikmalarni kimyo va munozara bilan bogʻlaydi.
why.ru: Большая часть текста перечисляет, чему Бобур научился в пекарне, а последнее предложение связывает эти навыки с химией и дебатами.

stem.en:
Each autumn, monarch butterflies in eastern North America fly south to spend the winter in central Mexico. Surprisingly, the butterflies that make this trip south are not the same ones that flew north months earlier. Instead, the return journey north is completed over several generations: butterflies lay eggs along the way, and their offspring continue the trip.

According to the text, how is the monarchs' journey north completed?

options.en: By several generations of butterflies, one after another
By the same butterflies that flew south to Mexico in the autumn
By only the youngest and strongest butterflies
In a single flight without any stops

why.en: The text says the trip north 'is completed over several generations': butterflies lay eggs and their offspring continue.
why.uz: Matnda shimolga safar «is completed over several generations» deyilgan: kapalaklar tuxum qoʻyadi, ularning avlodi yoʻlni davom ettiradi.
why.ru: В тексте сказано, что путь на север «is completed over several generations»: бабочки откладывают яйца, и потомство продолжает путь.

stem.en:
Kamila was nervous about her first piano recital. Her hands shook as she walked onto the stage, and for a moment she forgot how the piece began. Then she noticed her younger brother in the front row, waving and grinning. She smiled back, took a deep breath, and began to play. By the final notes, she had forgotten the audience entirely and was simply enjoying the music.

Which choice best describes what happens in the text?

options.en: A nervous performer is calmed by a familiar face and ends up enjoying the music.
A performer forgets how her piece begins and has to leave the stage before finishing.
A brother and sister perform a piano piece together for the first time.
A performer decides that she no longer wants to play in recitals.

why.en: Kamila starts nervous, her brother's wave calms her, and by the end she is 'simply enjoying the music'.
why.uz: Kamila avval hayajonlanadi, ukasining qoʻl silkitishi uni tinchlantiradi va oxirida u «simply enjoying the music».
why.ru: Камила сначала волнуется, брат машет ей и успокаивает её, и в конце она «simply enjoying the music».

stem.en:
Last fall, a school in the town of Oqtepa installed ten bicycle racks near its main entrance. Nodira, a student who writes for the school newspaper, claims that the racks have encouraged more students to ride bicycles to school.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Nodira's claim?

options.en: Before the racks were installed, about 5 students rode bicycles to school each day; a month later, about 25 did.
Most students at the school say that they prefer walking to school over riding a bicycle.
The bicycle racks were paid for by a business in the town.
Several teachers at the school drive to work every day.

why.en: Only the first finding shows bicycle riding rising after the racks appeared, which is what Nodira claims. The others are unrelated or point the other way.
why.uz: Faqat birinchi natija velosipedda kelish rastalar oʻrnatilgandan keyin koʻpayganini koʻrsatadi. Qolganlari aloqasiz yoki teskarisini koʻrsatadi.
why.ru: Только первый факт показывает рост числа велосипедистов после установки стоянок, как и утверждает Нодира. Остальные не связаны или противоречат.

stem.en:
The following text is from a short story. In it, the narrator describes her uncle Shavkat as a man who was generous with his time.

Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates this description?

options.en: "Whenever a neighbor needed help fixing a roof or moving furniture, my uncle put aside his own work and came at once."
"My uncle owned a small shop that sold tools, paint, and nails, and he kept it open six days a week, from dawn until dark."
"My uncle often said that he did not enjoy long conversations."
"Every summer, my uncle traveled alone to the mountains for a week of rest and quiet."

why.en: Being generous with time means giving it to others; only the first quotation shows him leaving his own work to help neighbors.
why.uz: Vaqtini ayamaslik uni boshqalarga berish demak; faqat birinchi iqtibosda u oʻz ishini qoldirib qoʻshnilariga yordam beradi.
why.ru: Щедрость на время — это отдавать его другим; только в первой цитате он бросает свои дела, чтобы помочь соседям.

stem.en:
Members of a school's nature club counted the birds that visited the feeder in the school garden during one week in each of three months.

Month | Birds counted in one week
October | 42
November | 57
December | 75

The club members noticed that the number of birds counted at the feeder ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

options.en: increased each month, from 42 in October to 75 in December.
decreased each month, from 75 in October to 42 in December.
was highest in November, when the club counted 57 birds at the feeder.
stayed about the same from October to December.

why.en: The counts go 42, 57, 75, so they rise each month. The other choices misread the order or the highest value.
why.uz: Sonlar 42, 57, 75: har oy oshib boradi. Qolgan javoblar tartibni yoki eng katta qiymatni notoʻgʻri oʻqiydi.
why.ru: Числа идут 42, 57, 75, то есть растут каждый месяц. Остальные ответы неверно читают порядок или наибольшее значение.

Dilnoza asked the students in her class how they usually travel to school.

Way of travel | Number of students
Walk | 12
Bus | 9
Car | 5
Bicycle | 4

Dilnoza concluded that walking is the most common way for students in her class to travel to school.

Which choice best describes data from the table that support Dilnoza's conclusion?

options.en: More students walk (12) than use any other way of travel.
Fewer students ride a bicycle (4) than travel by car (5).
Nine students in the class take the bus to school.
Walking and riding a bicycle together account for 16 students.

why.en: 'Most common' means the largest number: 12 walkers is more than any other group. The other choices are true but do not show this.

why.ru: «Most common» — самое большое число: 12 пешеходов больше любой другой группы. Остальные ответы верны, но этого не показывают.

stem.en:
Javohir planted two identical bean seeds in identical pots of soil. He put one pot on a sunny windowsill and the other in a dark closet, and he gave both pots the same amount of water each day. Because the only difference between the two pots was the amount of light each received, any difference in how the two plants grew ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: was most likely caused by the difference in light.
was most likely caused by the amount of water.
shows that the soil in one of the two pots was poor.
proves that bean plants need no light to grow.

why.en: Water, soil and seeds were the same; light was the only difference, so it is the most likely cause of any difference in growth.
why.uz: Suv, tuproq va urugʻ bir xil edi; faqat yorugʻlik farq qilgan, shuning uchun oʻsishdagi farqning eng ehtimoliy sababi yorugʻlik.
why.ru: Вода, почва и семена были одинаковыми, отличался только свет, поэтому именно он вероятнее всего вызвал разницу в росте.

stem.en:
The museum in Kamila's town is usually quiet on weekday mornings. Last Tuesday, however, the halls were crowded with children carrying notebooks and following a guide from room to room. Kamila's mother, who works at the ticket desk, said it was the busiest morning of the month. The crowd was most likely ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: a school group on a class visit.
a group of museum workers cleaning the halls.
tourists who had come for a weekend festival.
visitors waiting for the museum to close.

why.en: Children with notebooks following a guide on a weekday morning point to a school trip. Tuesday is not a weekend, and workers are not children.
why.uz: Ish kuni ertalab daftar koʻtargan bolalar gid ortidan yurgani maktab sayohatini bildiradi. Seshanba dam olish kuni emas.
why.ru: Дети с тетрадями, идущие за экскурсоводом утром в будний день, — это школьная экскурсия. Вторник не выходной.

stem.en:
The English word "algebra" comes from "al-jabr," a term in the title of a book by the scholar al-Khwarizmi, who worked at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad around 820. The word "algorithm" also comes from al-Khwarizmi, through Latin versions of his name. These two words, both common in mathematics and computer science today, suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: al-Khwarizmi's work has had a lasting influence on the language of mathematics.
al-Khwarizmi built the first computer while working in Baghdad.
most mathematical words in English come from the Latin language.
the House of Wisdom was mainly a school for language teachers.

why.en: Two everyday words of mathematics still come from his book and his name, which shows a lasting influence. Nothing in the text supports the others.
why.uz: Matematikaning ikki keng tarqalgan soʻzi hanuz uning kitobi va ismidan kelib chiqqan, bu uzoq taʼsirni koʻrsatadi. Boshqa javoblarga matnda asos yoʻq.
why.ru: Два ходовых слова математики до сих пор происходят от его книги и имени, это показывает долгое влияние. Другие ответы текстом не подтверждаются.
